Module boundaries exist as folders with an index.ts each
README has setup steps that work from a clean clone
`pnpm db:migrate` and `pnpm db:reset` work
A sample migration and a sample integration test pass in CI
Migrations are forward-only and run automatically on deploy
App refuses to start with a clear message when a required variable is missing

No secret has a production default
Workflow runs in under 10 minutes

Playwright report is uploaded on failure
`docker compose -f compose.prod.yml up` serves the app locally over Caddy

SvelteKit with adapter-node, TypeScript strict, pnpm, ESLint + Prettier, Vitest, Playwright. Use the current Node LTS and pin it in .nvmrc and the Dockerfile. Folder layout per ARCHITECTURE.md section 4 (src/lib/server/{auth,codes,content,events,analytics}, src/routes/{(student),(adult),(staff),api}).
compose.dev.yml with Postgres 16. Drizzle ORM with SQL migrations checked in. Test harness that gives each test file an isolated schema or transaction rollback so tests run in parallel.

Single config module that parses process.env with zod at boot and fails fast. .env.example documents every variable. Secrets (CODE_PEPPER, SESSION_SECRET, DATABASE_URL) never have defaults outside test.
GitHub Actions workflow on pull request and main. Postgres service container for integration tests. Playwright with Chromium and WebKit (iPad Safari stand-in). Cache pnpm. Fail on lint warnings.

Multi-stage Dockerfile, non-root user, healthcheck. compose.prod.yml with app, postgres (named volume), and Caddy as the only public service (automatic TLS, compression, static /media with Range support, access log disabled or IP-stripped). App and DB are not exposed on the host.

Staging VM in the chosen Canadian region. Firewall (22 from deploy source only, 80, 443), non-root deploy user, Docker. CI job: build image, push to registry, SSH deploy, run migrations, health-check gate. Staging shows a visible STAGING banner and uses its own secrets.
/healthz (process up) and /readyz (DB reachable, migrations current). JSON logs with request id, route, status, duration. Never log IP addresses, cookies, kit codes, join codes or request bodies.

Shared layout and CSS tokens. Body text at least 18px on student pages, tap targets at least 48px, WCAG AA contrast, system font stack (no third-party font requests), reduced-motion respected. Three route groups with distinct shells: student, adult, staff.
2026-11-14 Mike: pin Node 24 (.nvmrc and Dockerfile).

A deployable empty app: repo, CI, database, container image, and a live staging URL. Everything after this ships to staging on every merge, so deploy problems surface in week one instead of the week before the pilot.
- [ ] `pnpm dev`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm e2e` work from a clean clone
- [ ] CI is green and required on main
- [ ] Staging URL serves /healthz over HTTPS from a Canadian region

section: Rules that are not up for negotiation
text: 1. No accounts, names or free-text input for children. Ever.

section: Rules that are not up for negotiation
text: 2. When a kit's `logging_enabled` is false, the server stores nothing about that kit's activity. The `p6-nolog-invariant` test must never be skipped, weakened or deleted.

section: Rules that are not up for negotiation
text: 3. Class and kit identity come from the session, never from a request body.

section: Rules that are not up for negotiation
text: 4. Plain kit codes, join codes and tokens are never stored or logged. IP addresses are never stored or logged.

section: Rules that are not up for negotiation
text: 5. No request from the browser to any origin but our own. No third-party scripts, fonts, analytics or embeds.

section: Rules that are not up for negotiation
text: 6. Step IDs are permanent. A changed step gets a version bump; CI enforces it.

section: Rules that are not up for negotiation
text: 8. The decisions in `docs/adr/` stand. If one looks wrong, file a `decision` bead and stop.
- **Never start a bead labelled `human`.** If one blocks you, say so and stop, or pick other ready work.
- A bead is done when every acceptance criterion is met, tests pass locally and in CI, and the change is merged. Not before.
3. Implement with tests. Every new route goes into the authorization matrix test.
4. Run `pnpm lint && pnpm check && pnpm test && pnpm e2e`.
5. Commit with the bead ID in the message. Merge once CI is green; staging deploys itself.

section: Stop and ask the human when
text: - A secret, payment, DNS change or production deploy is needed.

One SvelteKit app (adapter-node, TypeScript strict) serves pages and API routes. Server code is split into `auth`, `codes`, `content`, `events`, `analytics` modules that talk through their `index.ts`.
PostgreSQL 16. Drizzle for typed queries. Migrations are SQL files, forward-only, run on deploy. Analytics is SQL views in the same database.
- Migrations stay compatible with the previous app version, so rollback to the previous image works
Production is a single Linux VM in a Canadian region running Compose: Caddy, app, Postgres. Staging is a second, smaller VM. Provider is a human decision (`p0-host`).
H.264/AAC MP4 at 720p with faststart, on a volume served by Caddy with Range support, behind short-lived signed URLs. No third-party video host.
Off means zero activity stored server-side.
- Pepper handling: p1-config (jade-8v4) reads `CODE_PEPPER` from config with no production default (jade-8v4 description)
No analytics, fonts, CDNs, embeds or error trackers that load in the user's browser. CSP enforces it and an e2e test asserts it.
Staging exists before feature work and is deployed on every merge to main. Production receives the image that passed staging.
pnpm, current Node LTS (pinned), ESLint + Prettier, Vitest, Playwright (Chromium and WebKit), GitHub Actions, zod, k6 for load.
A6: the repository has no git remote configured today (`git remote -v` is empty), so A6 is unconfirmed.
| Caddy | TLS, HTTP/2, compression, serves `/media` with Range requests | Only public service. Access log off or IP-stripped |
src/lib/server/{auth,codes,content,events,analytics}/   one folder per module, index.ts is its public API
src/routes/(student)/  (adult)/  (staff)/  api/
Modules call each other only through their `index.ts`. That is the whole "architecture enforcement" for a monolith this size.
| IP addresses as hidden identifiers | Not logged by Caddy or the app; used in memory for rate limiting only |
- **Environments:** local (Compose), staging (live from Phase 1, deployed on every merge to main), production (promoted by tag; same image that passed staging).
- **Releases:** build image, run forward-only migrations, start, health-check, switch. Rollback is the previous image. Migrations stay compatible with the previous app version.
Phase 2 and Phase 6 implement it as Drizzle schema plus SQL migrations.
The application's database role has `insert` and `select` on `events`, no `update`, and `delete` only through the `delete_kit_data(kit_id)` function added in Phase 9.
| Server logs | VM disk, 14 days | Every request | Staff with server access. No IPs, emails, codes, tokens or bodies |
Not collected at all: child names, photos, audio, free text from students, IP addresses, location, device identifiers, advertising identifiers, third-party cookies.
One VM and one object-storage bucket, both in Canada. No student traffic goes to any other company: no analytics service, no video platform, no font or script CDN, no error tracker in the browser.
- **TB1 Browser to Caddy.** Over the internet or school Wi-Fi, with TLS; only 80 and 443 are published (ARCHITECTURE.md section 10; p1-docker jade-80h).
- **TB2 Caddy to app.** The internal Compose network (ARCHITECTURE.md section 10); the Caddy access log is off or IP-stripped (ARCHITECTURE.md section 4; jade-80h).
- **TB9 Object storage to the staging VM.** Staging "uses its own secrets" (p1-staging jade-4zw; ADR 0014)
read through typed config with no production default (p1-config jade-8v4). Never in the database (ARCHITECTURE.md section 6)
| AB9 | IP addresses as hidden identifiers | Not logged by Caddy or the app (jade-80h, jade-alt, jade-ada); used in memory only, for rate limiting (jade-6cq; ADR 0020) |

| AB16 | A plain kit code leaking from the QR redeem URL (`/redeem?code=...`) into server logs or a Referer header (beyond ARCHITECTURE.md section 9) | App log lines contain no code values (jade-alt);

- The repository and CI path: GitHub is assumed (assumption A6 of `docs/adr/README.md`); code and content arrive through it, and content changes go through the same CI (ARCHITECTURE.md section 4; ADR 0006; p1-ci jade-xu0).
